verdict.rationale: Lium is a GPU rental platform, so user-defined background automations such as scheduled or triggered jobs are a fair axis to judge it on. The evidence shows no such feature. What it does offer is pod auto-removal on a TTL or spend cap, an SDK that runs a function once and tears the pod down, and APIs/CLI that an external agent can script. These are building blocks or adjacent lifecycle controls, not a product-provided automation that runs on its own schedule. The 6-hourly volume backups are a platform maintenance behavior, not user-configurable automation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
